Subject: ECA Revegetation
Comment: Correction 1: General Information  This project was reviewed for consistency with SMC 25.09.070: Standards for Vegetation and Impervious Surface Management. The proposed project activities appear to be located within mapped **steep slope environmentally critical areas (ECAs) and their buffers.       Revegetation requirements apply within **steep slope ECAs even if an exemption or other ECA relief is granted. The standards of SMC 25.09.070 apply when any of the following activities occur within **steep slope ECAs and their buffers: planting, disturbing, or removing trees and/or vegetation; adding, altering, or removing impervious surface; or other land disturbing activity. It appears that the revegetation requirements have not been *met. Please provide the following so we can determine the extent of tree and vegetation removal necessary and whether any impacts to ecological functions are adequately mitigated in the plan set.    Correction 2: Existing Conditions Sheet   1. C01: Include a note to "Reference sheet L002 for an existing tree table". Include tree identifiers on site plan for trees on-site and those that overhang from neighboring lots. 2. L001,L002, L003, L004: Remove buffer from drawings as the related exemption was approved for relief from prohibition of development. L002: Provide a summary in a brief narrative or bulleted list of the existing ecological functions performed by the Trees and vegetation within the ** steep slope ECA. The ecological functions include but may not be limited to: habitat for amphibian, avian, and terrestrial wildlife species; soil stabilization; and stormwater filtering, detention, and infiltration (SMC 25.09.065.C.2.a).  Correction 3: Project Impacts  1. L00: [25.09.065.C.2] Please provide a proposed site mitigation plan/table: Based on existing ground coverage, please show/delineate the proposed mitigation in the form of replanting. Determine the total area of impact that requires mitigation using the calculation (a+b=c):  a. Total new hard surface area  b. Total temporary construction disturbance area including all construction-related activities including, but not limited to construction access, staging area, temporary excavation, and areas of tree/vegetation removal.   c. Total area of impact that requires mitigation in the form of replanting. Calculations should only include areas within property lines, as we cannot approve information on the adjacent property.  Correction 4:  Proposed Mitigation  1. L004:  On the mitigation plan, show the location, size, species, quantities, and spacing of trees/shrubs to be newly planted. Use the ECA standard mitigation plan as a guide only. Seattle DPD Form - Standard Mitigation Plan   a. Shrub quantities can be determined by using multiplier 0.042 times the total area of impact that requires mitigation.   b. Tree replacement quantities can be 1:1. The goal is to provide a layered canopy.  c. References to help you choose native plants:  King County Native Plant Guide: Plant list - Native Plant Guide (kingcounty.gov) , WSU Native Plant Guide:WSU PNW Plants    2.  L004: Provide a summary in a brief narrative or bulleted list, an analysis of how the mitigation plan compensates for lost ecological functions within the ECA.    3.  L004: Add note stating: "Planting selections shall be Pacific Northwest native species suited to specific site conditions/orientation, no cultivars or hybrids are allowed." Verify.    4.  L004: Add note stating "New trees must be 4-6 feet in height and shrubs one-gallon size." Update proposed plant schedule as needed. 5.  L004: Add note stating "Areas that have been cleared, graded, or compacted are to be amended with organic matter prior to planting. Mulch, such as wood chips, should be added to a 3” thickness over the entire planting area without covering the stems of plants. " 6.  L004 (update existing note): Add note stating "The following monitoring and maintenance is required for a period of 5 years from date of plant installation. Self-monitoring is sufficient. No documentation is required to be submitted to SDCI unless requested.  a.  80 percent survival of new trees and vegetation planted at the end of five years;  b.  Annual inspections of the plants;  c.  Replacement of failed plants;  d.  Removal of exotic invasive species that have become established;   e. Photographic documentation of planting success retained for the five-year period; and  f. No permanent irrigation is allowed on steep slope areas or their buffers."Revegetation (1)

Please see the instructions below to complete this form. 1) The form must be signed by the owner or owner's representative; the form cannot be signed by the contractor nor the geotechnical engineer.      2) The Inspection Agency must be the same engineer/firm that prepared the geotechnical report. 3) If the owner nominates a different engineer/firm to act as the Geotechnical Special Inspector, the new engineer must review the original geotechnical report and submit a letter indicating a review was performed, along with a statement of agreement with the evaluation and provisions contained in the report. If the new engineer does not agree with aspects of the report, rebuttal evaluations and recommendations must be included in the review letter. The plans must be revised accordingly and submitted to SDCI for review. Requests for changes of Special Inspection Agency that occur during plan review should be submitted with corrected plans. If the request occurs after permit issuance, send the required documents to the geotechnical reviewer.

Comment: General: EHB 1848 / RCW 64.55 - Building Enclosure Law: Revised Code of Washington (RCW) 64.55.005 requires that the developers of multi-unit residential buildings comply with one of the three options listed below. Indicate which option will be used and provide electronic copies of the required documents as specified.  (1) a. Submit plans, details, and specifications for the construction of the building enclosure, per RCW 64.55.010(2). (2) Submit a completed, signed, and recorded Condominium Sales Prohibition Covenant which prohibits the sale of individual dwelling units as condominiums for a minimum of five years. The completed and signed form must be recorded with the King County Recorder ’s office and submitted prior to permit issuance, per RCW 64.55.020(10). Comment: Per 23.86.010.C.3, "On a lot with a rear property line, part of which is not essentially parallel to any part of the front lot line, the rear yard is measured from a line or lines drawn from side lot line(s) to side lot line(s), at least 10 feet in length, parallel to and at a maximum distance from the front lot line. If an alley abuts the rear of the property, 1/2 the width of the alley, between the side lot lines extended, is considered to be part of the lot for drawing this line. For those portions of the rear lot line that are essentially parallel to the front lot line, subsection 23.86.010.C.2 above shall apply. The lot depth is then measured perpendicularly from this 10 foot long line extended as needed to the point on the actual front lot line that is the furthest distance away. This establishes lot depth, which then may be used to determine the required rear yard depth." Since the rear lot line is not essentially parallel to the front lot line, please update rear yard accordingly.

Subject: DADUs & ADD/ALT less than 1500 S.F.
Comment: Sheet DWC: It appears from our mapping system that you would most likely be able to connect to an existing near side ditch/culvert in NE 125th Street. If this is not the case, and there is no ditch/culvert in NE 125TH street within frontage of this property, or this project is not able to discharge stormwater to this drainage ditch/culvert, then, the following is required: There is no available off-site point of discharge for drainage from this site. Where it has been determined by the Director that there is no off-site point of discharge (i.e. there is no public storm drainage system within the site frontage or that could be feasibly extended to the site) the project must infiltrate runoff from the area of development on-site. When infiltrating on-site, infiltration feasibility must first be demonstrated and the Drainage Control Plan (DWC Plan) must be prepared by a licensed Civil Engineer. In addition to meeting other minimum requirements for the project, the infiltration facility shall be designed to infiltrate the runoff volume from the area of development for the storm event with a 4 percent annual probability (25-year recurrence interval flow) and be sized so that overflows do not exceed 0.0001 cfs during the peak flow with a 4 percent annual probability (25-year recurrence flow). See Seattle Stormwater Manual, Volume 3, Section 4.3.2. Please submit the following with the next submittal … 1.Small Pilot Infiltration Test (Small PIT) Checklist and supporting documents prepared by a licensed Geotechnical Engineer*. 2.Drainage and Wastewater Control  Plan (DWC Plan) and Drainage Report prepared by a licensed Civil Engineer*.  3.Drainage Report with a continuous runoff stormwater model prepared by a licensed Civil Engineer*. *Note: for Infiltration testing and plan preparation clarification for detached accessory dwelling units (DADUs) and additions with less than 1,500 sf of new plus replaced hard surface on lots with No Off-site Point of Discharge:   The applicant is allowed to perform the infiltration testing unless otherwise determined by the Director.   If the applicant chooses (in lieu of a licensed professional) to conduct the infiltration testing, the applicant shall conduct the Small PIT (rather than the Simple Infiltration Test).   The test shall be documented with the Pilot Infiltration Test Checklist and a minimum 0.25 in/hr measured soil infiltration rate must be demonstrated.   Drywells shall be sized, at a minimum, per Appendix E-10 - Drywell Sizing Tables of the  Seattle Stormwater Manual.   The applicant is allowed to prepare the drainage control plan unless otherwise determined by the Director.Drainage (4)

Comment: General Information Note: Per SMC 22.807.020, drainage review is required when you are adding or replacing more than 750 square feet of hard surface along with other factors mentioned on the Stormwater Code website. Single-Family projects with 7,000 square feet or more of land disturbing activity, 1,500 square feet or more of new plus replaced hard surface or, if on a lot or parcel created or reduced in size on or after January 1, 2016, must implement On-site Stormwater Management (infiltration, dispersion, bio-retention, green roofs, permeable pavement, rainwater harvesting, etc.) to manage runoff from all hard surfaces on-site per SMC 22.805.030.B. and Director's Rule 21-2015.  This project is being reviewed under the 2021 Seattle Stormwater Code and Manual that went into effect July 1, 2021. Stormwater management requirements are based on the amount of new plus replaced hard surface (NPRHS) area associated with the project.  Examples of hard surfaces include roof areas with overhang/eaves, driveways, walkways, stairs, solid decking, patio and parking areas including pavement or gravel. Permeable pavement and pavers are also considered a hard surface.  When applicable, if decks and stairs are open slat and free draining to amended native soils below, please show and label as such on the Site Plan as well as the Drainage and Wastewater Control (DWC) Plan when applicable. If not open slat and free draining, these areas must be included as a hard surface within the OSM Calculator. Comment: OSM TREE REQUIREMENTS & NOTES – Surface #5 (stairs) Trees:  Trees must be onsite and within 20-feet of the entire impervious surface area to be eligible for GSI/OSM credit. Existing Trees:  On the DWC Plan; show and label the size and species of the existing trees to remain for GSI/OSM mitigation. The trees must have a minimum 6-inch diameter (as measured 4.5-feet above ground) and meet the requirements of section 4.4.2.2 of the Seattle Stormwater Manual Volume 3. On the DWC Plan, please also call the tree(s) out where they stand as “Required for OSM Surface #xxx ” making sure to reference the individual Surface number they are to mitigate per the OSM Calculator. New Trees: On the DWC Plan; show and label the size, species, and number the trees to be planted for GSI/OSM mitigation including the hard surface identifier the tree corresponds with per the OSM Calculator. Trees eligible for On-site Stormwater Management (OSM) must be on the City of Seattle Master Tree List: http://www.seattle.gov/Documents/Departments/SDOT/PublicSpaceManagement/2015-Street_Tree_List.p df Note: Trees in the "Small Category" are not eligible for mitigation. Deciduous must have a 1.5-inch minimum diameter as measured 6-inches above ground and evergreen trees must be a minimum of 4-feet tall and meet the requirements of section 5.2.4.2 and 5.2.5.2 of the 2016 Seattle Stormwater Manual Volume 3. On the DWC Plan, please also call the tree(s) out where they stand as “Required for OSM Surface #xxx ” making sure to reference the individual Surface number they are to mitigate per the OSM Calculator.  Tree Spacing:  In order to receive credit for GSI/OSM, the minimum tree spacing for newly planted trees shall accommodate mature tree spread as indicated in the City of Seattle Master Tree List http://www.seattle.gov/Documents/Departments/SDOT/PublicSpaceManagement/2015-Street_Tree_List.p df  Please provide spacing that matches the tree spread indicated on the Tree List.

Comment: Tree Replacement Requirements (SMC 25.11.090):  Tier 1, Tier 2, and Tier 3 trees removed in association with development must be replaced by one or more new trees designed to result, upon maturity, in a canopy cover that is at least roughly proportional to the canopy cover prior to tree removal. The proposed replacement trees (Bloodgood maple) does not meet these replacement requirements for the giant sequoia.  Please plant at least one evergreen conifer to provide proportional replacement for the giant sequoia. Incense cedar, Spanish fir, Serbian spruce or mountain hemlock would all be suitable replacement species.  Please refer to Director ’s Rule 12-2023 for more information about tree replacement requirements. Please note that the GreenFactor Plant list referenced in this rule only lists bioretention trees, which are only appropriate in wet areas. Comment: R402.4.1.3.1 Dwelling unit leakage rate. The maximum air leakage rate for any dwelling unit under any compliance path shall not exceed 4.0 air changes per hour. Comment: Informational for applicant on how to respond to city review comments: FOR INFORMATION ONLY.  In January 2022, SDCI transitioned to providing plan reviews via plan mark-up instead of traditional letters. We appreciate your understanding and patience as we rolled out the technology new to both applicants and SDCI staff.  The primary change that we are asking of applicants is that they document responses to comments directly in the plan set provided to them by SDCI at the end of each review cycle instead of sending letters corresponding to each correction letter. When all responses are documented, we ask that applicants upload the response plan set (as document type 'Correction Response Plan Set') along with the new, clean plan set as (document type 'Plan Set') for the next review cycle. This information is located at: https://www.seattle.gov/sdci/permits/how-to-respond-to-review-comments [If link is not active, cut and paste to URL] We have a video to help you learn how to navigate the new process here:  https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KB8laufkd7M. [If link is not active, cut and paste to URL] As we transition to delivering marked up plan sets, you may receive both letters and marked up plan sets with our corrections documented. As a rule, please respond to any marked-up plan set by embedding your responses in the marked-up plan set. We recognize that this transition requires changes to how you respond to our correction reports. We firmly believe that the changes we have instituted will lead to a reduction in the number of review cycles required to issue a permit. Remember, you will still: %ª Receive email notifications that a review has been completed. %ª Find review summary reports by discipline in the Seattle Services Portal as they are completed. %ª Updated plan sets can only be submitted after all reviews have been completed. What will be new is: %ª When all reviews are completed, you will receive a marked-up plan set which contains the comments from ALL the review disciplines. %ª Instead of preparing responses to each individual correction letter as you do today, you will be asked to reply to the comments directly in the marked-up plan set using either Bluebeam (requires a license) or Adobe Acrobat Reader (free).. %ª If you work with sub-consultants, you will need to coordinate with them to include their comments in your response plan set. Lastly, please help us perform reviews more efficiently! As we have worked on this transition, many of our reviewers indicated that they rely on bookmarks to navigate the (sometimes lengthy) plan sets that we receive from applicants. One thing that would allow us to review more quickly is to have applicants include a good set of bookmarks in every plan set that is submitted. Please follow the requirements for submitting pdf documents, outlined in Tip 106, General Standards for Plans and Drawings, [https://www.seattle.gov/DPD/Publications/CAM/cam106.pdf] to include a good set of bookmarks in every plan set you submit. NOTE: VERIFY THAT BOOKMARKS ARE NOT BROKEN PRIOR TO RESUBMITTING PLAN SETS. Bookmark links can become broken when sheets are added or removed from the plan set.01 Administration (3)

Comment: Informational for applicant on how to respond to city review comments: FOR INFORMATION ONLY.  In January 2022, SDCI transitioned to providing plan reviews via plan mark-up instead of traditional letters. We appreciate your understanding and patience as we rolled out the technology new to both applicants and SDCI staff.  The primary change that we are asking of applicants is that they document responses to comments directly in the plan set provided to them by SDCI at the end of each review cycle instead of sending letters corresponding to each correction letter. When all responses are documented, we ask that applicants upload the response plan set (as document type 'Correction Response Plan Set') along with the new, clean plan set as (document type 'Plan Set') for the next review cycle. This information is located at: https://www.seattle.gov/sdci/permits/how-to-respond-to-review-comments [If link is not active, cut and paste to URL] We have a video to help you learn how to navigate the new process here:  https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KB8laufkd7M. [If link is not active, cut and paste to URL] As we transition to delivering marked up plan sets, you may receive both letters and marked up plan sets with our corrections documented. As a rule, please respond to any marked-up plan set by embedding your responses in the marked-up plan set. We recognize that this transition requires changes to how you respond to our correction reports. We firmly believe that the changes we have instituted will lead to a reduction in the number of review cycles required to issue a permit. Remember, you will still: %ª Receive email notifications that a review has been completed. %ª Find review summary reports by discipline in the Seattle Services Portal as they are completed. %ª Updated plan sets can only be submitted after all reviews have been completed. What will be new is: %ª When all reviews are completed, you will receive a marked-up plan set which contains the comments from ALL the review disciplines. %ª Instead of preparing responses to each individual correction letter as you do today, you will be asked to reply to the comments directly in the marked-up plan set using either Bluebeam (requires a license) or Adobe Acrobat Reader (free).. %ª If you work with sub-consultants, you will need to coordinate with them to include their comments in your response plan set. Lastly, please help us perform reviews more efficiently! As we have worked on this transition, many of our reviewers indicated that they rely on bookmarks to navigate the (sometimes lengthy) plan sets that we receive from applicants. One thing that would allow us to review more quickly is to have applicants include a good set of bookmarks in every plan set that is submitted. Please follow the requirements for submitting pdf documents, outlined in Tip 106, General Standards for Plans and Drawings, [https://www.seattle.gov/DPD/Publications/CAM/cam106.pdf] to include a good set of bookmarks in every plan set you submit. NOTE: VERIFY THAT BOOKMARKS ARE NOT BROKEN PRIOR TO RESUBMITTING PLAN SETS. Bookmark links can become broken when sheets are added or removed from the plan set.01 Administration (3)

Comment: General Information Note: Per SMC 22.807.020, drainage review is required when you are adding or replacing more than 750 square feet of hard surface along with other factors mentioned on the Stormwater Code website. Single-Family projects with 7,000 square feet or more of land disturbing activity, 1,500 square feet or more of new plus replaced hard surface or, if on a lot or parcel created or reduced in size on or after January 1, 2016, must implement On-site Stormwater Management (infiltration, dispersion, bio-retention, green roofs, permeable pavement, rainwater harvesting, etc.) to manage runoff from all hard surfaces on-site per SMC 22.805.030.B. and Director's Rule 21-2015.  This project is being reviewed under the 2021 Seattle Stormwater Code and Manual that went into effect July 1, 2021. Stormwater management requirements are based on the amount of new plus replaced hard surface (NPRHS) area associated with the project.  Examples of hard surfaces include roof areas with overhang/eaves, driveways, walkways, stairs, solid decking, patio and parking areas including pavement or gravel. Permeable pavement and pavers are also considered a hard surface.  When applicable, if decks and stairs are open slat and free draining to amended native soils below, please show and label as such on the Site Plan as well as the Drainage and Wastewater Control (DWC) Plan when applicable. If not open slat and free draining, these areas must be included as a hard surface within the OSM Calculator. These notes and requirements are in lieu of establishing a formalized seasonal grading restriction on the project and constitute the customary requirements that would be instituted for a seasonal grading extension:   A site visit from the Geotechnical Special Inspector shall occur during each day of active grading and in the event of significant rainfall which might compromise stabilization measures between November 1 and March 31. The determination of what constitutes significant rainfall is subject to the discretion of the Geotechnical Special Inspector. However, as a minimum standard, the Geotechnical Special Inspector is required to conduct a site visit if more than one-half inch of precipitation occurs on any given day. Any recommendations required to maintain stability of excavations and proper functioning of the sediment/erosion control system provided by the Geotechnical Special Inspector and SDCI personnel shall be implemented immediately. The Geotechnical Special Inspector shall provide copies of field reports to SDCI Site Development Services Section no later than 48 hours after each inspection. The field reports may be emailed to sdcigeo@seattle.gov. The Geotechnical Special Inspector shall provide written notice that the site has been stabilized following completion of grading.

Comment: There is no available off-site point of discharge for drainage from this site. Where it has been determined by the Director that there is no off-site point of discharge (i.e. there is no public storm drainage system within the site frontage or that could be feasibly extended to the site) the project must infiltrate runoff from the area of development on-site. When infiltrating on-site, infiltration feasibility must first be demonstrated and the Drainage Control Plan (DWC Plan) must be prepared by a licensed Civil Engineer. In addition to meeting other minimum requirements for the project, the infiltration facility shall be designed to infiltrate the runoff volume from the area of development for the storm event with a 4 percent annual probability (25-year recurrence interval flow) and be sized so that overflows do not exceed 0.0001 cfs during the peak flow with a 4 percent annual probability (25-year recurrence flow). See Seattle Stormwater Manual, Volume 3, Section 4.3.2. Please submit the following with the next submittal … 1.Small Pilot Infiltration Test (Small PIT) Checklist and supporting documents prepared by a licensed Geotechnical Engineer*. 2.Drainage and Wastewater Control  Plan (DWC Plan) and Drainage Report prepared by a licensed Civil Engineer*.  3.Drainage Report with a continuous runoff stormwater model prepared by a licensed Civil Engineer*. *Note: for Infiltration testing and plan preparation clarification for detached accessory dwelling units (DADUs) and additions with less than 1,500 sf of new plus replaced hard surface on lots with No Off-site Point of Discharge:   The applicant is allowed to perform the infiltration testing unless otherwise determined by the Director.   If the applicant chooses (in lieu of a licensed professional) to conduct the infiltration testing, the applicant shall conduct the Small PIT (rather than the Simple Infiltration Test).   The test shall be documented with the Pilot Infiltration Test Checklist and a minimum 0.25 in/hr measured soil infiltration rate must be demonstrated.   Drywells shall be sized, at a minimum, per Appendix E-10 - Drywell Sizing Tables of the  Seattle Stormwater Manual.   The applicant is allowed to prepare the drainage control plan unless otherwise determined by the Director.DADUs & ADD/ALT less than 1500 S.F. Subject: Shoring system design
Comment: Repeated and revised item. SMC 22.170.110 A. Shoring system design calculations: The correction response memorandum from SSF, dated January 7, 2025, stated that the calculations for the shoring piles utilize ultimate passive pressure as an input in the Civil Tech program, with a separate safety factor of 1.2 applied. It seems there is some confusion between the safety factor and the ratio of ultimate to allowable design values. The soldier pile walls should use allowable passive pressure values, not ultimate or factored values. The results must demonstrate that the required safety factor is met using allowable passive pressure values of 175 pcf for the upper tier and 350 pcf for the lower tier. Revise the structural calculations accordingly.

Subject: General
Comment: General Information Note: Per SMC 22.807.020, drainage review is required when you are adding or replacing more than 750 square feet of hard surface along with other factors mentioned on the Stormwater Code website. Single-Family projects with 7,000 square feet or more of land disturbing activity, 1,500 square feet or more of new plus replaced hard surface or, if on a lot or parcel created or reduced in size on or after January 1, 2016, must implement On-site Stormwater Management (infiltration, dispersion, bio-retention, green roofs, permeable pavement, rainwater harvesting, etc.) to manage runoff from all hard surfaces on-site per SMC 22.805.030.B. and Director's Rule 21-2015.  This project is being reviewed under the 2021 Seattle Stormwater Code and Manual that went into effect July 1, 2021. Stormwater management requirements are based on the amount of new plus replaced hard surface (NPRHS) area associated with the project.  Examples of hard surfaces include roof areas with overhang/eaves, driveways, walkways, deck/patio and parking areas including pavement or gravel. Permeable pavement and pavers are also considered a hard surface.  When applicable, if decks and stairs are open slat and free draining to amended native soils below, please show and label as such on the Site Plan as well as the Drainage and Wastewater Control (DWC) Plan when applicable. If not open slat and free draining, these areas must be included as a hard surface within the OSM Calculator. Comment: General Information Note: Per SMC 22.807.020, drainage review is required when you are adding or replacing more than 750 square feet of hard surface along with other factors mentioned on the Stormwater Code website. Single-Family projects with 7,000 square feet or more of land disturbing activity, 1,500 square feet or more of new plus replaced hard surface or, if on a lot or parcel created or reduced in size on or after January 1, 2016, must implement On-site Stormwater Management (infiltration, dispersion, bio-retention, green roofs, permeable pavement, rainwater harvesting, etc.) to manage runoff from all hard surfaces on-site per SMC 22.805.030.B. and Director's Rule 21-2015.  This project is being reviewed under the 2021 Seattle Stormwater Code and Manual that went into effect July 1, 2021. Stormwater management requirements are based on the amount of new plus replaced hard surface (NPRHS) area associated with the project.  Examples of hard surfaces include roof areas with overhang/eaves, driveways, walkways, stairs, solid decking, patio and parking areas including pavement or gravel. Permeable pavement and pavers are also considered a hard surface.  When applicable, if decks and stairs are open slat and free draining to amended native soils below, please show and label as such on the Site Plan as well as the Drainage and Wastewater Control (DWC) Plan when applicable. If not open slat and free draining, these areas must be included as a hard surface within the OSM Calculator. Comment: General Drainage Review Information: Per SMC 22.807.020, drainage review is required when you are adding or replacing more than 750 square feet of hard surface along with other factors mentioned on the Stormwater Code website. Single-Family projects with 7,000 square feet or more of land disturbing activity, 1,500 square feet or more of new plus replaced hard surface or, if on a lot or parcel created or reduced in size on or after January 1, 2016, must implement On-site Stormwater Management (infiltration, dispersion, bio-retention, green roofs, permeable pavement, rainwater harvesting, etc.) to manage runoff from all hard surfaces on-site per SMC 22.805.030.B. and Director's Rule 21-2015.  This project is being reviewed under the 2021 Seattle Stormwater Code and Manual that went into effect July 1, 2021. Stormwater management requirements are based on the amount of new plus replaced hard surface (NPRHS) area associated with the project.  Examples of hard surfaces include roof areas with overhang/eaves, driveways, walkways, stairs, solid decking, patio and parking areas including pavement or gravel. Permeable pavement and pavers are also considered a hard surface.  When applicable, if decks and stairs are open slat and free draining to amended native soils below, please show and label as such on the Site Plan as well as the Drainage and Wastewater Control (DWC) Plan when applicable. If not open slat and free draining, these areas must be included as a hard surface within the OSM Calculator.  For reference/when applicable: Allowable Permeable Pavement Wearing Course Materials For Stormwater Credit: https://www.seattle.gov/Documents/Departments/SDCI/Codes/StormwaterSPUAllowablePermeablePavem ent.pdf  When drainage review is required, please ensure that you provide and are always using the most current and up to date drainage and sanitary sewer related plan, forms, and documents from the Stormwater Code page and 2021 Seattle Stormwater Manual available at https://www.seattle.gov/sdci/codes/codes-we-enforce-(a-z)/stormwater-code including:  As part of the complete plan set, a Drainage and Wastewater Control (DWC) Plan and Construction Stormwater Control and Post Construction Soil Management (CSC/Soil) Plan templates and/or standard plan notes. As a separate review document upload a PDF of the completed Onsite Stormwater Management (OSM) List Approach Calculator (version 01-04-2023 or newer) including the completed Site and Drainage Control Summary from the OSM Calculator on the DWC Plan. Updated standard plan BMP details on the DWC Plan or DWC Details Plan sheet when applicable. Comment: Footing drains do not appear to be required and/or proposed.  If they are not, on the DWC Plan – sheet C1.1, please remove DWC Plan Note #1D that says, “ROOF DRAIN LINES. TO BE KEPT SPEARATE FROM FOOTING DRAINS AT ALL TIMES WHEN PRESENT. ”   However, if footing drains are proposed/required then on the DWC Plan – sheet C1.1, please clearly show and label the perimeter foundation/footing drain discharge lines ( “FD” or “DRN ”) being routed directly to and passing through a catch basin prior to connecting to the onsite sanitary sewer connection to the combined sewer main. Comment: General Drainage Review Information: Per SMC 22.807.020, drainage review is required when you are adding or replacing more than 750 square feet of hard surface along with other factors mentioned on the Stormwater Code website. Single-Family projects with 7,000 square feet or more of land disturbing activity, 1,500 square feet or more of new plus replaced hard surface or, if on a lot or parcel created or reduced in size on or after January 1, 2016, must implement On-site Stormwater Management (infiltration, dispersion, bio-retention, green roofs, permeable pavement, rainwater harvesting, etc.) to manage runoff from all hard surfaces on-site per SMC 22.805.030.B. and Director's Rule 21-2015.  This project is being reviewed under the 2021 Seattle Stormwater Code and Manual that went into effect July 1, 2021. Stormwater management requirements are based on the amount of new plus replaced hard surface (NPRHS) area associated with the project.  Examples of hard surfaces include roof areas with overhang/eaves, driveways, walkways, stairs, solid decking, patio and parking areas including pavement or gravel. Permeable pavement and pavers are also considered a hard surface.  When applicable, if decks and stairs are open slat and free draining to amended native soils below, please show and label as such on the Site Plan as well as the Drainage and Wastewater Control (DWC) Plan when applicable. If not open slat and free draining, these areas must be included as a hard surface within the OSM Calculator. Subject: Grading Season Restriction Note
Comment: SMC 22.170.110 A.   Please add the following notes to the site plan. These notes and requirements are in lieu of establishing a formalized seasonal grading restriction on the project and constitute the customary requirements that would be instituted for a seasonal grading extension:   A site visit from the Geotechnical Special Inspector shall occur during each day of active grading and in the event of significant rainfall which might compromise stabilization measures between November 1 and March 31. The determination of what constitutes significant rainfall is subject to the discretion of the Geotechnical Special Inspector. However, as a minimum standard, the Geotechnical Special Inspector is required to conduct a site visit if more than one-half inch of precipitation occurs on any given day. Any recommendations required to maintain stability of excavations and proper functioning of the sediment/erosion control system provided by the Geotechnical Special Inspector and SDCI personnel shall be implemented immediately.  The Geotechnical Special Inspector shall provide copies of field reports to SDCI Site Development Services Section no later than 48 hours after each inspection. The field reports may be uploaded to the Geotechnical Special Inspection Account on the permit portal associated with this building permit application. The Geotechnical Special Inspector shall provide written notice that the site has been stabilized following completion of grading.

Subject: Special Inspector Nomination
Comment: SMC 22.170.130.  Nominate a geotechnical engineering firm on the enclosed SDCI Geotechnical Special Inspections Schedule form. This form must be signed by the owner or owner's representative; the form cannot be signed by the contractor nor the geotechnical engineer. The nomination form is available on the permit portal named "Special Inspection Notice".     The Inspection Agency must be the same engineer/firm that prepared the geotechnical report. If the owner nominates a different engineer/firm to act as the Geotechnical Special Inspector, the new engineer must review the original geotechnical report and submit a letter indicating a review was performed, along with a statement of agreement with the evaluation and provisions contained in the report. If the new engineer does not agree with aspects of the report, rebuttal evaluations and recommendations must be included in the review letter. The plans must be revised accordingly and submitted to SDCI for review. Please do not fill in special inspection items on the permit portal.     Requests for changes of Special Inspection Agency that occur during plan review should be submitted with corrected plans. However, the plans do propose a change to lot coverage with an increase in exterior stairs and landing area above 36" from grade being proposed for entrance to the AADU (SMC 23.44.010.D.2.c). The provided calculations remain inconsistent with the plans when measured to scale. Please address the following lot coverage items: i. The maximum lot coverage allowed calculation is incorrect. 5,462.6 x .35 is not equal to 1,912.91. Update this figure to 1,911.91.  ii. It appears the only change to lot coverage proposed in the cycle 4 plan set is the proposed reconfigured steps and landing areas leading to the 2nd level deck. It appears that, based on measurements of the site, that existing lot coverage exceeds the maximum allowed per Table B for SMC 23.44.010. Since maximum allowed lot coverage is likely already exceeded as the site currently exists, the proposed lot coverage figure will need to be equal to or less than the current lot coverage of the site per SMC 23.42.112. It appears areas of the upper floor of the structure that overlap with the lower floor may be counted twice in the provided calculations. Update the lot coverage calculations to  be measured from the footprint of all structures on the lot, from birds eye view. iv. The lot coverage figures provided are not closely aligning with the footprints of the structures as shown on the site plan when measured to scale (For example, the accessory structure measures out to 490 square feet, not 400 as the calculations suggest. This is the same for the other lot coverage areas as well). Update the plans to include lot coverage calculations and a lot coverage diagram that can be closely verified against the scaled plans. Additionally, clearly identify what areas are exempt from lot coverage and which areas are being counted toward lot coverage in accordance with SMC 23.44.010.D.2. Calculations should include any projections in excess of 36 ” including steps above 36" above grade per SMC 23.44.010.D.2. Subject: General Tree Comment
Comment: The Seattle City Council recently passed Council Bill 120534 establishing new tree protection requirements on private property in Seattle. The new regulations went into effect on July 30, 2023. Your application is subject to these new regulations, therefore information pertaining to trees on the subject property must be updated on the site plans. Additional information is needed to determine if the trees on site and trees off site with canopies/roots extending onto the site require retention or protection from construction activity per SMC 25.11. Provide location, species, and diameter at 4.5 feet above the ground of all Tier 1, Tier 2, Tier 3, and Tier 4 trees, including off-site trees with canopies overhanging and/or roots extending onto the development site. Please also provide tree protection area and fencing per SMC 25.11.060.A for all Tier 1, Tier 2, and Tier 3 trees that will be retained during development. SDCI ’s Tree and Vegetation Protection Detail must be included in the plan set: https://www.seattle.gov/Documents/Departments/SDCI/Codes/TreeDetail.pdf  Refer to Tip 242 A for further information  https://www.seattle.gov/DPD/Publications/CAM/Tip242A.pdf Replacement of removed tier 1,2 and 3 tree is required per Directors rule 12-2023 and code section 25.11.090. If trees are proposed for removal that meet these categories show replacement on the site plan, showing Genus and species and add the following note in relation to the replacement tree/s: Please add the following text in relation to the proposed replacement trees..   For each relocated or required replacement tree, maintenance and monitoring is required for a five-year period. The period begins when the replacement tree is planted. Maintenance and monitoring shall include the following: 1.Sufficient maintenance actions to ensure survival of the replacement tree: a. When more than one replacement tree is required, 80 percent survival of new trees planted at the end of five years; b. When one replacement tree is required, 100 percent survival of the new tree planted at the end of five years; 2.Replacement and replanting of failed trees; and 3.Photographic documentation of planting success retained for the five-year period. Submission of documentation to the Seattle Department of Construction and Inspections is not Genus and required unless requested by the Department. Per the requirements of Directors rule 12-2023   indicate the proposed method of irrigation for the replacement trees on the plan setPaul Humphries (1)

Comment: As proposed, this appears to be a partially below grade basement being labeled as "garage" in order to exempt it from DADU square footage allowances found in SMC 23.44.041. Subject: Scooter garage
Comment: Third request As proposed, this appears to be a partially below grade basement being labeled as "garage" in order to exempt it from DADU square footage allowances found in SMC 23.44.041. Table A, letter f. The intent of the code is not to permit the relabeling of an entire ~875 sq ft basement to garage in order to exempt the area unless it is a bona fide garage. Scooter garages are permitted by code and can include incidental utility functions such as water heaters and similar.  That said, the "garage" designation cannot be used in a indiscriminate manner to exempt out an entire floor in order for it to be within the allowances for a DADU.  Please revise by proposing a scooter garage that does not encompass the entire basement.   If you have further questions, please email me to set up a time to discuss. Zoning (1)

Subject: General
Comment: General Information Note: Per SMC 22.807.020, drainage review is required when you are adding or replacing more than 750 square feet of hard surface along with other factors mentioned on the Stormwater Code website. Single-Family projects with 7,000 square feet or more of land disturbing activity, 1,500 square feet or more of new plus replaced hard surface or, if on a lot or parcel created or reduced in size on or after January 1, 2016, must implement On-site Stormwater Management (infiltration, dispersion, bio-retention, green roofs, permeable pavement, rainwater harvesting, etc.) to manage runoff from all hard surfaces on-site per SMC 22.805.030.B. and Director's Rule 21-2015.  This project is being reviewed under the 2021 Seattle Stormwater Code and Manual that went into effect July 1, 2021. Stormwater management requirements are based on the amount of new plus replaced hard surface (NPRHS) area associated with the project.  Examples of hard surfaces include roof areas with overhang/eaves, driveways, walkways, deck/patio and parking areas including pavement or gravel. Permeable pavement and pavers are also considered a hard surface.  When applicable, if decks and stairs are open slat and free draining to amended native soils below, please show and label as such on the Site Plan as well as the Drainage and Wastewater Control (DWC) Plan when applicable. If not open slat and free draining, these areas must be included as a hard surface within the OSM Calculator. Subject: Zoning – SMC 23.44 – Single-Family Residential
Comment: The proposed DADU appears to encroach slightly into the required south side yard. Per Table A for SMC 23.44.041, Letter H, a detached accessory dwelling unit may not be located within the side yard required by subsection 23.44.014.B except as provided in subsection 23.44.014.C.3 or 23.44.014.C.4, and footnote 4 of Table A for SMC 23.44.041. Additionally SDCI DR 4-2019 states, “for purposes of yard or setback standards, measurement shall be taken to the outside surface of the building foundation rather than to exterior finishing such as siding, provided that the finishes extend no more than 6 inches into a required yard or setback ”. Update the plans to demonstrate the proposed DADU is outside of the required south side yard in accordance with Table A for SMC 23.44.041, Letter H and SDCI DR 4-2019 (https://www.seattle.gov/dpd/codes/dr/DR2019-4.pdf).

Subject: Zoning – SMC 23.44 – Single-Family Residential
Comment: The provided lot coverage calculations appear to be incorrect. Per SMC 23.44.010.D.2, decks or parts of a deck that are 36 inches or less above existing grade as well as the first 36 inches of eaves and gutters that project from principal and accessory structures are exempt from lot coverage (i.e. most of section J on the DADU lot coverage diagram should be exempt area). Update the lot coverage diagrams to label and dimension all eaves and gutters for both the existing and proposed structures and clearly identify the first 36 ” of all eaves/gutter projections as exempt from lot coverage. Any eave/gutter projections in excess of 36 ” should be counted toward lot coverage. Additionally, it does not appear the existing steps that are above 36 ” from existing grade are being appropriately counted toward lot coverage. Update the lot coverage diagrams and calculations accordingly. Note, the outer most side of the posts that support the existing entry covering to the primary residence should be used to determine the wall plane. The eave/gutter projections less than 36" from the invisible wall line formed between the post supports are exempt from lot coverage per SMC 23.44.010.D.2.

Subject: Zoning – SMC 23.44 – Single-Family Residential
Comment: The elevations label maximum base height for the proposed DADU. However, parts of the DADU appear to exceed base height that are not otherwise a pitched, butterfly, or shed roof nor do they appear to meet any of the allowed projections in the footnotes of Table A for SMC 23.44.041. Base height is the point at which the vertical face of low side (west) of the structure meets the top of the sloped roof line. It appears that point on the plans is approximately 11" above max base height. Update the plans to clearly demonstrate that only the slope above vertical face of the structure exceeds max base height in accordance with Table for SMC 23.44.041 Letter k and Exhibit A for SMC 23.44.041.

Incense cedar, Spanish fir, Serbian spruce or mountain hemlock would all be suitable replacement species.  Please refer to Director ’s Rule 12-2023 for more information about tree replacement requirements. Please note that the GreenFactor Plant list referenced in this rule only lists bioretention trees, which are only appropriate in wet areas. Comment: General Information Note: Per SMC 22.807.020, drainage review is required when you are adding or replacing more than 750 square feet of hard surface along with other factors mentioned on the Stormwater Code website. Single-Family projects with 7,000 square feet or more of land disturbing activity, 1,500 square feet or more of new plus replaced hard surface or, if on a lot or parcel created or reduced in size on or after January 1, 2016, must implement On-site Stormwater Management (infiltration, dispersion, bio-retention, green roofs, permeable pavement, rainwater harvesting, etc.) to manage runoff from all hard surfaces on-site per SMC 22.805.030.B. and Director's Rule 21-2015.  This project is being reviewed under the 2021 Seattle Stormwater Code and Manual that went into effect July 1, 2021. Stormwater management requirements are based on the amount of new plus replaced hard surface (NPRHS) area associated with the project.  Examples of hard surfaces include roof areas with overhang/eaves, driveways, walkways, stairs, solid decking, patio and parking areas including pavement or gravel. Permeable pavement and pavers are also considered a hard surface.  When applicable, if decks and stairs are open slat and free draining to amended native soils below, please show and label as such on the Site Plan as well as the Drainage and Wastewater Control (DWC) Plan when applicable. If not open slat and free draining, these areas must be included as a hard surface within the OSM Calculator.  For reference/when applicable: Allowable Permeable Pavement Wearing Course Materials For Stormwater Credit: https://www.seattle.gov/Documents/Departments/SDCI/Codes/StormwaterSPUAllowablePermeablePavem ent.pdf  When drainage review is required, please ensure that you provide and are always using the most current and up to date drainage and sanitary sewer related plan, forms, and documents from the Stormwater Code page and 2021 Seattle Stormwater Manual available at https://www.seattle.gov/sdci/codes/codes-we-enforce-(a-z)/stormwater-code including:  As part of the complete plan set, a Drainage and Wastewater Control (DWC) Plan and Construction Stormwater Control and Post Construction Soil Management (CSC/Soil) Plan templates and/or standard plan notes. As a separate review document upload a PDF of the completed Onsite Stormwater Management (OSM) List Approach Calculator (version 01-04-2023 or newer) including the completed Site and Drainage Control Summary from the OSM Calculator on the DWC Plan. Updated standard plan BMP details on the DWC Plan or DWC Details Plan sheet when applicable. Comment: OSM TREE REQUIREMENTS – for Surface #4 (driveway) Trees:  Trees must be onsite and within 20-feet of the entire impervious surface area to be eligible for GSI/OSM credit. Deciduous must have a 1.5-inch minimum diameter as measured 6-inches above ground and evergreen trees must be a minimum of 4-feet tall and meet the requirements of section 5.2.4.2 and 5.2.5.2 of the 2016 Seattle Stormwater Manual Volume 3. Comment: Based on measurements of the proposed DADU floor plans, it appears to exceed Gross Floor Area (GFA) limits. Per Table A letter f for SMC 23.44.041, the gross floor area of a detached accessory dwelling unit may not exceed 1,000 square feet excluding garage and exterior-only accessed storage areas, covered porches and covered decks that are less than 25 square feet in area, and gross floor area that is underground. Up to 35 square feet of floor area dedicated to long-term bicycle parking shall be exempt from the gross floor area calculation for a detached accessory dwelling unit. Update the plans to include gross floor area diagrams and calculations for the structure that demonstrate compliance with Table A for 23.44.041, letter F. GFA should be measured from the interior face of the exterior walls (see Director ’s Rule 4-2019, https://www.seattle.gov/dpd/codes/dr/DR2019-4.pdf ). The GFA diagrams and calculations should account for the attached garage as exempt gross floor area in accordance with Table A for SMC 23.44.041. Any raised covered porch/patio/deck/entry in excess of 25 square feet should be counted toward GFA. If 25 square feet or less, such covered porches/patios/decks/entries should be identified as exempt.

Comment: Correction 1: General Information  This project was reviewed for consistency with SMC 25.09.070: Standards for Vegetation and Impervious Surface Management. The proposed project activities appear to be located within mapped **steep slope and potential landslide prone environmentally critical areas (ECAs) and their buffers.       Revegetation requirements apply within **steep slope and potential landslide prone ECAs even if an exemption or other ECA relief is granted. The standards of SMC 25.09.070 apply when any of the following activities occur within ECAs and their buffers: planting, disturbing, or removing trees and/or vegetation; adding, altering, or removing impervious surface; or other land disturbing activity. It appears that the revegetation requirements have not been *met. Please provide the following so we can determine the extent of tree and vegetation removal necessary and whether any impacts to ecological functions are adequately mitigated in the plan set.    Correction 2: Existing Conditions Sheet  (A1.1) 1. Provide an existing conditions plan. Clearly show the ** steep slope and potential landslide prone ECAs and their buffers on the existing conditions plan.  Public facing GIS mapping tool, helpful for viewing property and generating a site plan with required information: ArcGIS Web Application  2. Provide a brief description/identification of the existing ground coverage (prior to work done without permits) within the area of temporary and permanent disturbance in the ECA. Examples of ground coverage include: lawn, ornamental landscaping (vegetation species), blackberry or other invasive species, tree species, patio, pathway, driveway, stairway, etc. Calculate the area in square footage and show this on the existing conditions plan.  3. Show locations of all existing trees located within and adjacent to the disturbance area consistently across all plan view sheets. Include a tree table with genus, species, common name, DSH (diameter at standard height), dripline diameter and if trees/vegetation are proposed to remain or be removed. Please number trees consistently within table and across all plan view sheets. Do not include tier categories for trees in ECAs. 4. Provide a summary in a brief narrative or bulleted list of the existing ecological functions performed by the trees and vegetation within the ** steep slope and potential landslide prone ECA. The ecological functions include but may not be limited to: habitat for amphibian, avian, and terrestrial wildlife species; soil stabilization; and stormwater filtering, detention, and infiltration (SMC 25.09.065.C.2.a). Subject: General
Comment: General Information Note: Per SMC 22.807.020, drainage review is required when you are adding or replacing more than 750 square feet of hard surface along with other factors mentioned on the Stormwater Code website. Single-Family projects with 7,000 square feet or more of land disturbing activity, 1,500 square feet or more of new plus replaced hard surface or, if on a lot or parcel created or reduced in size on or after January 1, 2016, must implement On-site Stormwater Management (infiltration, dispersion, bio-retention, green roofs, permeable pavement, rainwater harvesting, etc.) to manage runoff from all hard surfaces on-site per SMC 22.805.030.B. and Director's Rule 21-2015.  This project is being reviewed under the 2021 Seattle Stormwater Code and Manual that went into effect July 1, 2021. Stormwater management requirements are based on the amount of new plus replaced hard surface (NPRHS) area associated with the project.  Examples of hard surfaces include roof areas with overhang/eaves, driveways, walkways, deck/patio and parking areas including pavement or gravel. Permeable pavement and pavers are also considered a hard surface.  When applicable, if decks and stairs are open slat and free draining to amended native soils below, please show and label as such on the Site Plan as well as the Drainage and Wastewater Control (DWC) Plan when applicable. If not open slat and free draining, these areas must be included as a hard surface within the OSM Calculator.  For reference/when applicable: Allowable Permeable Pavement Wearing Course Materials For Stormwater Credit: https://www.seattle.gov/Documents/Departments/SDCI/Codes/StormwaterSPUAllowablePermeablePavem ent.pdf  When drainage review is required, please ensure that you provide and are always using the most current and up to date drainage and sanitary sewer related plan, forms, and documents from the Stormwater Code page and 2021 Seattle Stormwater Manual available at https://www.seattle.gov/sdci/codes/codes-we-enforce-(a-z)/stormwater-code including:  As part of the complete plan set, a Drainage and Wastewater Control (DWC) Plan and Construction Stormwater Control and Post Construction Soil Management (CSC/Soil) Plan templates and/or standard plan notes. As a separate review document upload the completed Onsite Stormwater Management (OSM) List Approach Calculator (version 01-04-2023 or newer) including the completed Site and Drainage Control Summary from the OSM Calculator on the DWC Plan. Updated standard plan BMP details on the DWC Plan or DWC Details Plan sheet when applicable. Subject: Tree Replacement Requirements (SMC 25.11.090)
Comment: Updated: Zoning requirements are separate from replacement requirements under 25.11.090. Incense cedar, coast redwood, Douglas fir, or western red cedar may all be appropriate replacement trees. New trees must replace (at maturity) the canopy cover removed, so more than one replacement tree may be needed, depending on the species chosen. Repeated: Removal of trees 814 and 813 (if approved) must meet tree replacement requirements. Tier 1, Tier 2, and Tier 3 trees removed in association with development must be replaced by one or more new trees designed to result, upon maturity, in a canopy cover that is at least roughly proportional to the canopy cover prior to tree removal. Replacement trees must also be native and/or culturally significant, and resilient to climate change (SMC 25.11.090.C.2). Please refer to Director ’s Rule 12-2023 for more information about tree replacement requirements. Please note that the GreenFactor Plant list referenced in this rule only lists bioretention trees, which are only appropriate in wet areas. Please choose a drought-tolerant species. Feel free to email me with species selection questions.

Comment: Drainage Review is required for this project per the 2021 Seattle Stormwater  Manual Volume 1, Chapter 8, since there is 750 square feet or more of new plus replaced hard surface and/or 5,000 square feet or more of land disturbing activity. Please complete and submit the following documents: 1) Standard Construction Stormwater Control and Soil Amendment  (CSC/SOIL) Plan 2) Standard Drainage and Wastewater Control (DWC) Plan 3) On-site Stormwater Management (OSM) List Approach Calculator (full workbook) 4) Infiltration Evaluation Documentation / Infiltration Test Checklist The following are the Approved Points of Discharge for the project: a) The "Approved Point of Stormwater Discharge" is "On-site Infiltration". b) The "Drainage Basin" is "N/A for Single Family Projects". c) The "Approved Point of Wastewater Discharge" is "Public Sanitary Sewer" d) The "Approved Point of Subsurface Discharge" is "On-site Infiltration". Subject: DADUs & ADD/ALT less than 1500 S.F.
Comment: There is no available off-site point of discharge for drainage from this site. Where it has been determined by the Director that there is no off-site point of discharge (i.e. there is no public storm drainage system within the site frontage) the project must infiltrate runoff from the area of development on-site. When infiltrating on-site, infiltration feasibility must first be demonstrated and the Drainage Control Plan (DWC Plan) must demonstrate that all runoff up to the 25-year recurrence interval is infiltrated on-site, or, if not feasible, all runoff is dispersed on-site using a dispersion BMP per the Seattle Stormwater Manual, Volume 3, Section 4.3.2. Please submit the following with the next submittal … 1.Small Pilot Infiltration Test (Small PIT) Checklist and supporting documents prepared by a licensed Geotechnical Engineer***. 2.Drainage and Wastewater Control  Plan (DWC Plan) and Drainage Report prepared by a licensed Civil Engineer***.  3.Drainage Report with a continuous runoff stormwater model prepared by a licensed Civil Engineer***. ***Note: for Infiltration testing and plan preparation clarification for detached accessory dwelling units (DADUs) and additions with less than 1,500 sf of new plus replaced hard surface on lots with No Off-site Point of Discharge:   The applicant is allowed to perform the infiltration testing unless otherwise determined by the Director.   If the applicant chooses (in lieu of a licensed professional) to conduct the infiltration testing, the applicant shall conduct the Small PIT (rather than the Simple Infiltration Test).   The test shall be documented with the Pilot Infiltration Test Checklist and a minimum 0.25 in/hr measured soil infiltration rate must be demonstrated.   Drywells shall be sized, at a minimum, per Appendix E-10 - Drywell Sizing Tables of the  Seattle Stormwater Manual.   The applicant is allowed to prepare the drainage control plan unless otherwise determined by the Director. Subject: Seismic Site Class justification
Comment: The uploaded geotechnical report assumed Site Class D to determine seismic coefficients. To categorize the site as Site Class D, please demonstrate one of the following criteria: a) Shear wave velocity for the top 100 ft is between 600 and 1,200 ft/s. b) SPT-N blow counts for the top 100 ft are between 15 and 50 per foot. c) Undrained shear strength for the top 100 ft is between 1,000 and 2,000 lb/ft². The subsurface explorations presented in the uploaded geotechnical report lack sufficient detail to determine the site class. As per Section 11.4.3 of ASCE 7-16, when soil properties are not known in sufficient detail to determine the site class, Site Class D is selected as the default site class, and the value of Fa shall not be less than 1.2.  Please revise the seismic design parameters in the geotechnical report and update the structural design calculations accordingly.

Comment: Shear Wall H/L Adjustment Factors S-2.X Calcs 16 & 17 SDPWS 4.3.3 Clarify how the shear wall capacities/stiffness/force distribution have been adjusted for their stiffness for walls sharing force in a line. S2.0 SW107 Please include calculations for SW105 &107, as they  appear to be FTAO have piers that need to have reductions based on stiffness. Response Per the exception to section 4.3.3.4.1 of the SDPWS, the unit shear in full height qualifying panels may be taken as proportional to the shear capacity for different shearwalls within a shear line.   Based on our design, the unit shear within the full height panels for shearwall 105 and 107(310 plf and 365 plf, respectively) are within acceptable tolerances to be considered proportional to their capacity (both are 3" on center edge nailing).  Therefore it is our professional opinion that the distribution of shear force within this shear line meets the intent of the NDS and no further action is required. Subject: Engineered Lateral
Comment: Overturning Calculation and no holdown at SW 202 Calcs 13 This comment is for reference and no response is required. It is made because the calculation shown appears to be non-conservative for walls with H/L>1.0. The calculations of forces in the wall show an addition of a horizontal force to the vertical force, and the force applied Emh does not appear to be correlated to E (possible issue with the spreadsheet). The OT calcs do not appear to follow the principles of statics with horizontal forces added to vertical forces. Please clarify how the forces have been added considering he locations directions of forces. Response Per ASCE 7-16 Section 12.14.3.2, Em = Emh + Ev  Emh is the effect of a horizontal seismic force, not the actual horizontal force in the wall. The horizontal force causes a vertical force at the end of a wall due to a moment couple. The principles of statics apply as a vertical force is being added to another vertical force. Cycle 2 The calculations do not follow the principles of statics per the original comment and our conference call on 7/7. Repeat comment. Include each force as a vector.

Comment: If you intend to reuse existing side sewer, an Evaluation and Certification of the existing side sewers by a Professional Engineer is necessary because the existing side sewer/s were installed prior to 2004.   SS Code 21.16.240 and the Requirements for Design and Construction of Side Sewers Director's Rule (DR 4-2011) detail the requirements for use of an existing side sewer. In summary, a civil engineer must evaluate and certify the existing side sewer; if the side sewer is 50 years or older, the side sewer will need to be lined; if the existing side sewer is less than 50 years old, the side sewer must either be lined or the Evaluation and Certification process must include a pressure test. Please add  a very clear, boxed note added to the Drainage and Wastewater Control Plan that  the existing side sewer must be Evaluated and Certified by a Professional Engineer and either rehabilitated (i.e. lined) or pressure tested all the way to the public mainline in the street.  The completed Evaluation and Certification form must be submitted to the inspector during construction.  The form is available with the following link: http://www.seattle.gov/dpd/permits/permittypes/sidesewer/default.htm

Comment: The plans state the proposed garage for the single family residence is detached, however, this garage appears to be attached. Per Director ’s Rule 10-95, an accessory structure is detached from a principal structure if it is not physically connected to the other structure. Subject: Zoning – SMC 23.44 – Single-Family Residential
Comment: The FAR diagrams do not include diagrams for the existing single family residence (SFR). Update the plans to include floor area calculations and diagrams for each level of the entire structure that accurately depict the gross floor area of the structure and account for any exempt floor area per SMC 23.44.011.  Take special note of the exemptions to floor area in single family residences contained in SMC 23.44.011.C.  Please also see SMC 23.86.007 and its exhibits as well as SDCI DR 4-2019 at http://www.seattle.gov/dpd/codes/dr/DR2019-4.pdf for additional information on how to measure the floor area of a structure. The floor area diagrams must include the interior dimensions used to calculate the area and provide an accompanying table showing the use of space or level, amount of gross floor area and identify whether it is chargeable or exempt gross floor area. If exemption 23.44.011.C.2 or 1 can be applied, the elevations should label and dimension the height above grade from existing or finished grade (whichever is lower) to the basement ceiling. Comment: General Information Note: Per SMC 22.807.020, drainage review is required when you are adding or replacing more than 750 square feet of hard surface along with other factors mentioned on the Stormwater Code website. Single-Family projects with 7,000 square feet or more of land disturbing activity, 1,500 square feet or more of new plus replaced hard surface or, if on a lot or parcel created or reduced in size on or after January 1, 2016, must implement On-site Stormwater Management (infiltration, dispersion, bio-retention, green roofs, permeable pavement, rainwater harvesting, etc.) to manage runoff from all hard surfaces on-site per SMC 22.805.030.B. and Director's Rule 21-2015.  This project is being reviewed under the 2021 Seattle Stormwater Code and Manual that went into effect July 1, 2021. Stormwater management requirements are based on the amount of new plus replaced hard surface (NPRHS) area associated with the project.  Examples of hard surfaces include roof areas with overhang/eaves, driveways, walkways, stairs, solid decking, patio and parking areas including pavement or gravel. Permeable pavement and pavers are also considered a hard surface.  When applicable, if decks and stairs are open slat and free draining to amended native soils below, please show and label as such on the Site Plan as well as the Drainage and Wastewater Control (DWC) Plan when applicable. If not open slat and free draining, these areas must be included as a hard surface within the OSM Calculator.  For reference/when applicable: Allowable Permeable Pavement Wearing Course Materials For Stormwater Credit: https://www.seattle.gov/Documents/Departments/SDCI/Codes/StormwaterSPUAllowablePermeablePavem ent.pdf  When drainage review is required, please ensure that you provide and are always using the most current and up to date drainage and sanitary sewer related plan, forms, and documents from the Stormwater Code page and 2021 Seattle Stormwater Manual available at https://www.seattle.gov/sdci/codes/codes-we-enforce-(a-z)/stormwater-code including:  As part of the complete plan set, a Drainage and Wastewater Control (DWC) Plan and Construction Stormwater Control and Post Construction Soil Management (CSC/Soil) Plan templates and/or standard plan notes. As a separate review document upload a PDF of the completed Onsite Stormwater Management (OSM) List Approach Calculator (version 01-04-2023 or newer) including the completed Site and Drainage Control Summary from the OSM Calculator on the DWC Plan. Updated standard plan BMP details on the DWC Plan or DWC Details Plan sheet when applicable. C) Maximum shear is anticipated to be between the compression load and the tension load in the shearwall. Clarify how the shear in the foundaiton was designed for this force. Comment: General Information Note: Per SMC 22.807.020, drainage review is required when you are adding or replacing more than 750 square feet of hard surface along with other factors mentioned on the Stormwater Code website. Single-Family projects with 7,000 square feet or more of land disturbing activity, 1,500 square feet or more of new plus replaced hard surface or, if on a lot or parcel created or reduced in size on or after January 1, 2016, must implement On-site Stormwater Management (infiltration, dispersion, bio-retention, green roofs, permeable pavement, rainwater harvesting, etc.) to manage runoff from all hard surfaces on-site per SMC 22.805.030.B. and Director's Rule 21-2015.  This project is being reviewed under the 2021 Seattle Stormwater Code and Manual that went into effect July 1, 2021. Stormwater management requirements are based on the amount of new plus replaced hard surface (NPRHS) area associated with the project.  Examples of hard surfaces include roof areas with overhang/eaves, driveways, walkways, deck/patio and parking areas including pavement or gravel. Permeable pavement and pavers are also considered a hard surface.  When applicable, if decks and stairs are open slat and free draining to amended native soils below, please show and label as such on the Site Plan as well as the Drainage and Wastewater Control (DWC) Plan when applicable. If not open slat and free draining, these areas must be included as a hard surface within the OSM Calculator. Comment: General Information Note: Per SMC 22.807.020, drainage review is required when you are adding or replacing more than 750 square feet of hard surface along with other factors mentioned on the Stormwater Code website. Single-Family projects with 7,000 square feet or more of land disturbing activity, 1,500 square feet or more of new plus replaced hard surface or, if on a lot or parcel created or reduced in size on or after January 1, 2016, must implement On-site Stormwater Management (infiltration, dispersion, bio-retention, green roofs, permeable pavement, rainwater harvesting, etc.) to manage runoff from all hard surfaces on-site per SMC 22.805.030.B. and Director's Rule 21-2015.  This project is being reviewed under the 2021 Seattle Stormwater Code and Manual that went into effect July 1, 2021. Stormwater management requirements are based on the amount of new plus replaced hard surface (NPRHS) area associated with the project.  Examples of hard surfaces include roof areas with overhang/eaves, driveways, walkways, stairs, solid decking, patio and parking areas including pavement or gravel. Permeable pavement and pavers are also considered a hard surface.  When applicable, if decks and stairs are open slat and free draining to amended native soils below, please show and label as such on the Site Plan as well as the Drainage and Wastewater Control (DWC) Plan when applicable. If not open slat and free draining, these areas must be included as a hard surface within the OSM Calculator. Subject: General Tree Comment
Comment: Based on the drip line of existing trees and the proposed project, it does not appear that any excavation and/or construction-related activity will occur within the tree protection areas of any on- or off-site trees. SDCI's standard tree and vegetation protection is not required. Please clearly note on the site plan a defined "development impact area." The development impact area is the area on the site affected by proposed site improvements, site access, storage/stockpiling of materials, or construction activities such as grading, filling, trenching, or other excavation necessary to install utilities or access. Include the following note on the site plan : Tree Protection/Development Impact Area Requirements: (1) Retention and protection of all trees 6 inches or greater is required. (2) No tree removal or damage is authorized. (3) Excavation and ground disturbance is prohibited outside of the development impact area. (4) Construction-related activities, such as site access, heavy equipment use, storage, or stockpiling is prohibited outside of the development impact area unless located on existing hard surfaces.Paul Humphries (1)

Subject: General
Comment: General Information Note: Per SMC 22.807.020, drainage review is required when you are adding or replacing more than 750 square feet of hard surface along with other factors mentioned on the Stormwater Code website. Single-Family projects with 7,000 square feet or more of land disturbing activity, 1,500 square feet or more of new plus replaced hard surface or, if on a lot or parcel created or reduced in size on or after January 1, 2016, must implement On-site Stormwater Management (infiltration, dispersion, bio-retention, green roofs, permeable pavement, rainwater harvesting, etc.) to manage runoff from all hard surfaces on-site per SMC 22.805.030.B. and Director's Rule 21-2015.  This project is being reviewed under the 2021 Seattle Stormwater Code and Manual that went into effect July 1, 2021. Stormwater management requirements are based on the amount of new plus replaced hard surface (NPRHS) area associated with the project.  Examples of hard surfaces include roof areas with overhang/eaves, driveways, walkways, deck/patio and parking areas including pavement or gravel. Permeable pavement and pavers are also considered a hard surface.  When applicable, if decks and stairs are open slat and free draining to amended native soils below, please show and label as such on the Site Plan as well as the Drainage and Wastewater Control (DWC) Plan when applicable. If not open slat and free draining, these areas must be included as a hard surface within the OSM Calculator.  For reference/when applicable: Allowable Permeable Pavement Wearing Course Materials For Stormwater Credit: https://www.seattle.gov/Documents/Departments/SDCI/Codes/StormwaterSPUAllowablePermeablePavem ent.pdf  When drainage review is required, please ensure that you provide and are always using the most current and up to date drainage and sanitary sewer related plan, forms, and documents from the Stormwater Code page and 2021 Seattle Stormwater Manual available at https://www.seattle.gov/sdci/codes/codes-we-enforce-(a-z)/stormwater-code including:  As part of the complete plan set, a Drainage and Wastewater Control (DWC) Plan and Construction Stormwater Control and Post Construction Soil Management (CSC/Soil) Plan templates and/or standard plan notes. As a separate review document upload the completed Onsite Stormwater Management (OSM) List Approach Calculator (version 01-04-2023 or newer) including the completed Site and Drainage Control Summary from the OSM Calculator on the DWC Plan. Updated standard plan BMP details on the DWC Plan or DWC Details Plan sheet when applicable. Subject: Performance Monitoring Notes
Comment: SMC 22.170.110 A.  Given the depth of proposed excavation and the close proximity of temporary shoring to adjacent properties and structures, please include the shoring monitoring notes to reflect the following SDCI minimum monitoring requirements:  (1) Indicate on the plan the minimum monitoring point spacing along the top of the wall and minimum distance behind the wall per the geotechnical engineer's recommendations.  (2) Establish a baseline reading of monitoring points on the ground surface and settlement-sensitive structures behind the shoring wall alignment prior to dewatering, excavation, and installation of the shoring systems.   (3) A licensed surveyor (not the contractor) must do the surveying at least once a week.   (4) Survey frequency can be decreased after the shoring system has been installed and excavation is complete if the data indicates little or no additional movement. Surveying must continue until the permanent structure (including floor slabs as braces) is complete up to final and street grades. The survey frequency will be determined by the geotechnical engineer after review and approval by SDCI and SDOT.   (5) The geotechnical engineer shall review survey data and provide an evaluation of wall performance along with survey data to SDCI and SDOT on at least a weekly basis. Immediately and directly, notifyv SDCI and SDOT if any unusual or significantly increased movement occurs.   (6) Immediately and directly notify the geotechnical and structural engineers, wall designer, SDCI, and SDOT if 0.5 inches of movement occurs between two consecutive readings and when total movements reach 0.5 inch. At that amount of movement, the engineers and designers shall determine the cause of displacement and develop remedial measures sufficient to limit total wall movements to 1 inch. All earthwork and construction activities must be directed towards immediate implementation of remedial measures necessary to limit total wall movements to what has been defined as acceptable by the design team and SDOT (as indicated above).
